newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-up $0.50-trade.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-up $0.50-trade.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hog prices Tuesday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt higher, lifted by expectations for strong packer demand, livestock dealers said.
Several hog slaughtering and pork processing plants were closed Monday in observance of the Veterans Day holiday.
Those packers closed will be needing hogs for Tuesday operations, which could increase competition among all packers for live hog inventories, the dealers said.
Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to the plant could range from $53.50 to $54.50 per cwt and top plant prices in Illinois could range from $53.50 to $54.00.
Indiana/Ohio top hog prices at the plant could range from $52.00 to $53.00, possibly $53.50, the dealers said.
Hog prices also could be bolstered by strong pork prices and expectations for continued strength Tuesday following light pork production on Monday.
Carlot pork prices Monday were up $2.00 to $4.00 per cwt for skinned hams and up $2.00 for pork bellies, according to USDA. There were 25.1 pork loads and 6.0 loads of pork trimmings sold.
